newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end soft on Wall St, regional bolsas.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end soft on Wall St, regional bolsas.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed weaker with the market dragged down by Wall Street's slide and slumps in other Latin American markets, said dealers.
The bearish mood is seen continuing at the opening with investors concerned by the brewing trade dispute over import rules between Brazil and its Mercosur partners.
"Tomorrow looks black. The headlines will knock the stock market down further," said one trader.
The 40-share index ended down 0.8 percent at 113.62 points. The general index shed 0.35 percent at 5,277.54 points on volume of 13.3 billion pesos.

Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) closed sharply lower in line with the Dow, which tumbled on fears the Federal Reserve will raise U.S. interest rates again to quash inflation, said dealers.
The Santiago bourse was also hurt by sharp slides in the Buenos Aires and the Brazilian bolsas, they said.
Dealers said local players were concerned by the row sparked by Brazil's decision to impose new import finance rules, which are seen as an indirect way of reducing imports.
Investors were also using the uncertainty in the bolsa to cash in gains from the bolsa's bull run at the start of the year, they said.
Declines included bottler Andina, down 2.73 percent at 2,490 pesos, telecom CTC, down 2.35 percent at 2,905 pesos and pulp-maker Copec, which lost 1.4 percent to 1,548 pesos.
Winners included copper products manufacturer Madeco, up 1.92 percent at 1,060 pesos, forestry firm Masisa, up 0.55 percent at 211-1/6 pesos and telecom Entel which rose 0.34 percent at 2,960 pesos.
